note: Three 30 s scripts in the new chain structure, written by hand for the owner's review (2026-10-25, $0). Facts are only ones already verified in earlier runs. Not from the creator's scripts.

sentences.text: If you hang one red lamp over a crossing, you have a traffic light.
But it never changes, so cars pile up down both roads.
So you add a green lamp and a gray box that switches them.
This is a signal controller.
But the box runs on a clock, so at midnight a lone car sits at an empty red.
So you bury a loop of wire in the road that feels a car's metal.
But now the light flips the instant a car arrives, and a car already crossing gets hit.
So you add a yellow lamp that gives everyone a few seconds to stop.
And many of those sensors are wire loops, not cameras.
Add a crosswalk, a bench, and a mailbox.
Congratulations, you have built a traffic light.

chain.shows: cars queue at the red lamp down both roads, the queue growing
night, one car waiting at a red light with nobody else around
the light snaps green under an arriving car while a crossing car is mid-junction, near miss
chain.stakes: a car hit in the junction

sentences.text: If you dig a ditch along your house, you have a drain.
But one inch of rain on a roof dumps over 600 gallons, and the ditch overflows.
So you fill the ditch with gravel to hold the water.
But now the gravel holds that water against the wall, and the wall cracks.
So you lay a pipe full of holes under the gravel, sloping away downhill.
This is a French drain.
But mud washes into the gravel, clogs every hole, and the basement floods anyway.
So you wrap the gravel in fabric that keeps the mud out.
And the French in French drain is not France.
It is Henry French, who wrote the book on drains in 1859.
Add the grass back on top.
Congratulations, you have built a French drain.

chain.shows: rain pours off the roof, the ditch brims and spills against the wall
water sits in the gravel at the wall, a crack runs up the foundation
mud fills the pipe's holes, water rises inside the basement
chain.stakes: the basement and everything in it

sentences.text: If you spray a muddy car with a hose, you have a car wash.
But the mud just smears on the paint.
So you build an arch with soap sprays and spinning brushes.
But now soapy, oily water runs off the lot and into the creek.
So you cut a floor drain into an underground tank.
This is a water reclaim tank.
But the tank fills to the brim, and dirty water backs up over the floor.
So you add a pump that sends up to 80 percent back to the arch.
And a car wash does not waste more water than your hose.
It uses about 45 gallons a car, while a hose can top 100.
Add a pay kiosk and a canopy.
Congratulations, you have built a car wash.

chain.shows: brown mud streaks across the paint under the hose
grey foamy water runs off the lot, down the street and into the creek
chain.stakes: the creek and what lives in it

chain.shows: the tank brims and dirty water wells up over the wash floor
